beats.text: This is jaiscloud, a local emulator for Google Cloud. We point real Google clients, and real Terraform, at it, and run one crypto data product through its whole life.
Provision. Terraform creates the buckets, the KMS key, the feed secret and the Pub/Sub topic. Then gcloud creates the Managed Kafka cluster, the Dataproc cluster and the rest of the data platform.
Ingest. A bridge pod reads a live public trade feed, normalizes every trade, and produces it to Managed Kafka, a real Redpanda broker running inside the cluster.
Process. One always-on Spark job on Dataproc reads Kafka and writes the medallion: raw bronze, parsed and deduplicated silver, and a windowed gold table in Iceberg on the Hive Metastore.
Serve. Every gold rollup fires Eventarc, which drives a Cloud Run publisher into Firestore and BigQuery, and this leaderboard re-sorts live as each window lands.
Observe and automate. A custom metric crosses an alert policy and opens an incident on Pub/Sub, while Cloud Scheduler submits the batch rollup on a cron. All of it, locally.
